title: Back from vacation with broken shoulders: Returning to my AI MUD to find a Zombie apocalypse!
author: Least-Monk-131
selftext:
Hey everyone, been a minute. Back to the daily grind after an awesome trip to Portugal with my 12 yo kid. I went full beast mode all vacation and, of course, came back with my shoulders absolutely wrecked. So now, my free time is basically 100% dad duties, coding my AI text MUD, and trying to lift through some nasty tendon inflammation (currently experimenting with every kind of kinesio tape known to man 😭).

Before I left, I had built out the foundations of the world using just a few procedural commands. Stuff like this:

`# THE CENTER: HEGEMONY OF MYCENAE (0, 0)` `build_kingdom 25 35 20 150000 TEMPERATE monumental 0 0 "Hegemony of Mycenae" "The Wanax" "Mycenae" "The Acheron" "A brutal and powerful hegemony..."`

`# THE EAST: DOMINION OF KHEM (15, -8)` `build_kingdom 20 40 25 200000 DESERT monumental 40 -0 "Dominion of Khem" "The Dark Pharaoh" "Shadow Thebes" "Desert of Seth" "An ancient and corrupted desert dominion..."`

(Plus Thule, the Phoenician Confederation, Troy, etc.)

With just a handful of lines, the engine populated a massive world full of kings, queens, guards, and commoners going about their lives.

Well... I came back from vacation and logged in, only to find a wasteland of dead souls and zombies. All my poor non-player people were dead, starving, dying of thirst, or had turned into zombies in a desolate world! To be honest though, the zombies were actually pretty chill—just talking about this and that while drinking at the tavern!

I’m trying to make the NPCs feel truly alive—instead of just standing there waiting for input, they defend themselves, go to the tavern, end up destitute, and literally starve to death if they can't find food. Before I left, I decided the standard city plagues weren't cutting it anymore, so I added a zombie outbreak to the world; it’s incredible to watch an NPC survive abject misery, only to get bitten and turn two days later. The AI ​​handled everything else while I was away.

Oh, I’m also experimenting with storing Lua scripts directly in the database. Basically, you can add custom scripts to any NPC or object to give them unique behaviors. I want anyone to be able to build their own world—their own kingdom—simply by providing generic descriptions. It doesn't have to be an ancient world; it could be set in the future or the present day.

The best part? I’m setting it up so that players with the right permissions (and tokens) can modify and reuse them. It’s essentially a built-in multiplayer modding system. I’m also working on generating black-and-white, "gamebook-style" illustrations for room backgrounds—they add an incredible atmosphere. The crazy thing? It’s all still running locally on my poor mini-PC (Ryzen 7 5600, 32 GB of RAM).

As you know from my previous posts, I’m using my usual RabbitMQ/Docker/pgvector setup to keep the system asynchronous, but handling all these new mechanics at once makes the CPU scream like an F1 car!!! ...And that’s just while I’m playing it by myself!!!

But all in all, the system is holding up well! Next goal: create an "Underworld" where deceased players are sent, forcing them to fight to reclaim their loot.

The game isn't open to the public yet; if I launched it right now, my poor Ryzen 7 would literally melt down. I want to keep the infrastructure strictly local rather than relying on the cloud, which means that sooner or later, I’ll need to build a more powerful home server to handle real players. If you’d like to support this crazy project, help fund a hardware upgrade, or simply buy me more kinesiology tape, check out the Patreon page:[https://www.patreon.com/homeris](https://www.patreon.com/homeris). The posts are completely free! I’m also setting up a Discord server for the upcoming Alpha phase—it’s a work in progress, so keep an eye out for the link in the next update!
